findings.summary: F4 does not actually verify the engine-authoritative revision and is timing-flaky. The test creates git repo `d`, records `sha = rev-parse HEAD` of `d`, then calls `runDispatch({allowedRoot: d, gitDir: true})`. Because `gitDir: true` makes the helper discard the passed `allowedRoot` and substitute a second, freshly created repo, the payload's `revision` comes from a DIFFERENT repository than the one `sha` was read from. Both repos are built by `makeGitDir()` with an identical tree (`f.txt` = "x\n"), no parent, identical author/committer `t <t@t>` and identical message, so their commit SHAs are equal only when both commits land in the same integer second — i.e. the assertion passes by accidental SHA collision, not because the engine resolved HEAD of the configured `allowed_root`. This makes F4 non-discriminating (spec §3.1/§3.2: a criterion that passes for the wrong reason is not evidence) and makes the suite intermittently red, so F15 (full suite exit 0) does not reliably hold. Fix: drop `gitDir: true` at the call site (or read `sha` from the repo the helper actually used, returned as `gitDir`).

Root cause of the F4 defect: the `gitDir` branch in the shared `runDispatch` helper unconditionally overwrites the caller-supplied `allowedRoot` with a newly created repo instead of promoting an existing one, so `allowedRoot` and `gitDir` are silently mutually exclusive. Any future test passing both will observe the same shadowing.
